subject: sr-business-studies
title: Planning and Organising
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a step in the planning process?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: It may create a false sense of security among employees, as activities will take place as per plan. This is a limitation of —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Identification of the activities to be performed is the first step of which process?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The active process of entrusting a part of work, authority and creating accountability is called —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The function of management which bridges the gap between where we are and where we want to go is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an importance of planning?
questions.answer: C

Selecting course, identifying alternatives, objectives, assumptions
questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Give one-word answers with respect to types of plans: (i) These clearly indicate what is to be done and what is not to be done in a given situation. (ii) A general statement that guides decision making.
questions.answer: (i) Rules. (ii) Policy.

questions.q: Name the organisational concepts: (i) The framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed. (ii) A systematic effort to delegate authority to all levels of management and in all departments.
questions.answer: (i) Organisational structure. (ii) Decentralisation.

questions.q: State true or false: (b) A strategy is a general statement that guides decision-making. (c) Policies are plans which determine the sequence of any work performance. (d) Budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms.
questions.answer: (b) False – policy. (c) False – procedure. (d) True.

questions.q: Name the function of management: Alliance Ltd's departments coordinate and authority–responsibility relationships are established with clarity of reporting. (also give its importance)
questions.answer: Organising; it leads to specialisation and clarity of authority and responsibility.

questions.q: Identify the types of plans: (a) End results towards which activities are directed. (b) Plan prepared considering competitors' moves.
questions.answer: (a) Objectives. (b) Strategy.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Planning is the ______ function of management and is ______ (looks ahead).
questions.answer: primary (first); futuristic.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Planning is a continuous process. (ii) Informal organisation is created by top management.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False.

questions.q: Give the three elements of delegation.
questions.answer: Assignment of responsibility, granting authority and creating accountability.

questions.q: Name any two modern organisational structures.
questions.answer: Team structure and matrix structure (also network structure).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: 'A CEO retains only the authority to decide on opening new branches and delegates all other decision-making powers.' Identify and give the meaning of the concept of management being followed.
questions.answer: Decentralisation: a systematic effort to delegate authority at all levels and in all departments, shifting decision-making power to lower levels.

questions.q: Employees feel demotivated due to excessive emphasis on strict rules and regulations. Identify the type of organisation whose limitation is highlighted and explain its meaning.
questions.answer: Formal organisation: an officially established pattern of relationships created by management with defined authority, rules and procedures, which can be rigid.

questions.q: Lalit joins a firm; workers form a hockey club after work. Which type of organisation is the hockey club? Give one limitation.
questions.answer: Informal organisation; limitation: it can spread rumours and may resist changes.

questions.q: Identify and give the meaning of the process that is the ultimate outcome of planned delegation.
questions.answer: Decentralisation: systematic delegation of authority to all levels of management and in all departments.

questions.q: Is planning probabilistic? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes; planning is based on forecasts and assumptions about the future, which may not come true, so plans may need revision.

questions.q: State any two limitations of planning.
questions.answer: It leads to rigidity and does not work in a dynamic environment; it is time consuming and expensive.

questions.q: What is meant by organisational structure?
questions.answer: The framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed, a network of job positions and authority relationships.

questions.q: What is a policy? Give an example.
questions.answer: A general statement that guides decision-making; e.g. training only candidates who scored above 60 per cent.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the relationship between planning and controlling.
questions.answer: Planning sets objectives and standards; controlling compares actual results with them and corrects deviations. Planning provides the base for control, and control provides feedback for revising plans: planning looks ahead, controlling looks back.

questions.q: Explain: (a) Planning is pervasive (b) Planning is a continuous process (c) Planning is futuristic.
questions.answer: (a) Needed at all levels and in all functions. (b) Done again and again as plans are made and revised. (c) Concerned with deciding in advance what to do in the future.

questions.q: Explain: (a) Objectives (b) Strategy (c) Policy.
questions.answer: Objectives are end results; strategy is a comprehensive plan considering competitors' moves; policy is a general statement guiding decisions.

questions.q: Briefly explain: (a) Policy and (b) Rules as types of plans.
questions.answer: A policy is a general guide to decision making within boundaries; a rule clearly states what must or must not be done in a situation, with penalty for violation.

questions.q: Explain any three importance of planning.
questions.answer: It provides direction, reduces risk and uncertainty and facilitates decision making and control.

questions.q: Distinguish between formal and informal organisation (three points).
questions.answer: Formal is created by top management, authority from position and permanent; informal arises spontaneously, authority from personal qualities and temporary.

questions.q: Explain the importance of delegation (three points).
questions.answer: It reduces workload, improves managerial effectiveness and develops subordinates with motivation.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define Centralisation and Decentralisation. Distinguish between them.
questions.answer: Centralisation keeps decision-making authority at top levels; decentralisation systematically delegates authority at all levels. Differences: delegation is compulsory, decentralisation optional; scope narrow versus wide; responsibility shared in decentralisation only; purpose to lessen burden versus to increase subordinates' role.

questions.q: 'Planning is looking ahead, Controlling is looking back.' Analyse and explain the statement.
questions.answer: Planning decides in advance objectives and ways of achieving them; controlling compares actual results with plans and takes corrective action after performance; both are interdependent: planning provides standards, controlling provides feedback.

questions.q: Explain the steps in the process of planning.
questions.answer: Establishing objectives, making assumptions (premises), identifying alternatives, evaluating alternatives, selecting a course of action, implementing the plan, and review and follow-up.

questions.q: Explain the process of organising.
questions.answer: Identification of activities, grouping them into departments, assignment of duties, granting authority and establishing authority-responsibility relationships for coordination.

questions.q: What is meant by delegation? Briefly explain its elements.
questions.answer: Delegation is entrusting work and authority to another with accountability; elements: assignment of responsibility, granting authority and creating accountability.

questions.q: Briefly explain any five points of importance of planning.
questions.answer: Gives direction, reduces risk and uncertainty, coordination, facilitates decision-making, economy and efficiency and control.

questions.q: Explain the importance of organising.
questions.answer: It leads to specialisation, optimum use of resources, clarity of authority, creativity, growth, coordination and adaptation to change.
